sections.title: Physics/Chemistry
sections.note: Basic physics/chemistry questions, not including device physics or basic circuit physics which have their own sections.

sections.title: General Power Supply
sections.note: Assume DC-DC for nearly every question unless specified or implied. AC power supplies are rarely brought up during my interviews given their use cases and relevance to my experience.

sections.title: Buck Converters
sections.note: Buck converter board routing is in PCB Design/Layout section. I often refer to the "on state" where the high-side FET is on and the diode/low-side FET is off and the "off state" where the high-side FET is off and the diode/low-side FET is on.

sections.title: Power Bridge
sections.note: Many of these questions assume that synchronous rectification is implemented, but some also compare the behavior/performance between a low-side NFET and diode.

path: Debugging, Validating, and Characterizing Buck Converters
sections.title: Debugging, Validating, and Characterizing Buck Converters
Boost Converters
sections.note: Many of the boost converter questions can be similar to bucks, but I barely have any experience with boosts so they aren't covered as much in my interviews.

sections.title: Inductive Loads
sections.note: Mostly on DC inductive loads like brushed DC motors and solenoids. I've only been asked a tiny bit of AC inductive loads in the context of brushless motors. Most of these questions arise because of my personal projects with motors and solenoids, only a few roles I've interviewed for actually use motors/solenoids. I was also asked most of these questions during my freshman year before I started taking interview notes and before I had any internship or school experience, so these questions are mostly from memory. Most of these questions will be for motors (since I've been asked mostly about them), but there's a good amount of overlap with solenoids.

sections.title: Single-Phase Inductive Drives
sections.note: PCB design/layout on inductive drives is in the PCBs section.

sections.title: Half/H-Bridge
sections.note: There's a good amount of overlap with the Power Bridge subsection of Buck Converters as well, since the power bridge of a buck is often just a half bridge.

sections.title: Control from Embedded Device
sections.note: Often times you want to control a big motor/solenoid from a small embedded device. This section focuses on some of the more power electronics side of things while the Embedded Systems section will focus a bit more on the embedded side of things.

sections.title: Sense Resistor
sections.note: Sense resistor PCB layout/routing is in PCB Design/Layout section

sections.title: High-Speed Signals
sections.note: Diff pairs and high-speed design from board layout/design perspective, as opposed to signals or SI perspective. Diff pairs are often used for high-speed signals, so there will be a good amount of overlap with the Transmission Lines (TL) section, especially microstrip TLs.

sections.title: Transmission Line Effects
sections.note: Transmission line (TL) effects on a PCB/microstrip transmission line, also lots of overlap with TL section.

sections.title: Power Supply-Level Layout and Placement
sections.note: Mostly dealing with switching power supplies as they present additional layout and routing challenges. Tons of overlap with the previous High-Current Layout/Routing as power supplies often need to supply lots of current.
